title: US Announces New Tariffs on Major Trading Partners
subtitle: President Trump’s latest trade policy aims to protect American jobs, but experts warn of higher prices for consumers.

summary.en: The United States government has announced a new series of taxes on goods imported from several countries. These taxes, known as tariffs, will affect major partners including China, the European Union, and Taiwan. The White House claims these measures will help American workers and fix unfair trade practices. However, many economists are worried that these policies could lead to higher prices for everyday shoppers. The new rules are not expected to start until next year and will likely face legal challenges.
summary.zh: 美國政府宣布對多國進口商品徵收一系列新稅。這些稱為關稅的稅款將影響包括中國、歐盟與台灣在內的主要貿易夥伴。白宮聲稱這些措施將有助於美國勞工並修正不公平的貿易行為。然而，許多經濟學家擔心這些政策可能導致一般消費者的物價上漲。新規則預計要到明年才會實施，且極可能面臨法律挑戰。

paragraphs.en: The United States government has announced a new series of taxes on products imported from many countries around the world. These taxes, known as tariffs, are fees that businesses must pay to the government when they bring goods into the country. This move is part of President Donald Trump’s plan to change how the US trades with other nations. The new policy will affect many of America’s biggest trading partners, including China, the European Union, Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan.
paragraphs.zh: 美國政府宣布對全球多國進口的產品徵收一系列新稅。這些稅款稱為關稅，是企業在將商品運入國內時必須支付給政府的費用。此舉是川普 (Donald Trump) 總統改變美國與其他國家貿易方式計畫的一部分。這項新政策將影響美國許多主要的貿易夥伴，包括中國、歐盟、日本、南韓以及台灣。

paragraphs.en: According to BBC Business, the US Trade Representative (USTR) announced these proposed taxes after conducting a long investigation into the trade practices of other countries. The government claims that for many years, these nations have used unfair strategies to help their own businesses. Jamieson Greer from the USTR stated that these new tariffs are designed to “level the playing field” for American workers. The US government argues that some countries have kept wages low and used other unfair methods to gain an advantage, which has hurt the manufacturing industry in the United States.
paragraphs.zh: 根據 BBC 商業新聞報導，美國貿易代表署 (USTR) 在對其他國家的貿易行為進行長期調查後，宣布了這些擬議的稅收。政府聲稱，多年來這些國家一直採取不公平的策略來協助本國企業。來自美國貿易代表署的葛瑞爾 (Jamieson Greer) 表示，這些新關稅旨在為美國勞工「創造公平的競爭環境」。美國政府主張，部分國家長期壓低工資並使用其他不公平手段來獲取優勢，這已損害了美國的製造業。

paragraphs.en: Under this new plan, different countries will face different tax rates. China is facing the highest potential tariff rate of up to 40%, while Vietnam could face up to 35%. Other countries, including those in the European Union and several nations in Asia, are looking at rates of 20% or 25%. President Trump has long argued that these measures are necessary to boost local manufacturing and create more jobs for Americans. He also hopes to reduce the US trade deficit, which is the difference between the value of goods a country buys from others and the value of goods it sells to them.
paragraphs.zh: 根據這項新計畫，不同國家將面臨不同的稅率。中國面臨的潛在關稅稅率最高，可達百分之四十，而越南可能面臨高達百分之三十五的稅率。其他國家，包括歐盟成員國及亞洲多個國家，則面臨百分之二十或二十五的稅率。川普長期以來主張，這些措施對於提振在地製造業及為美國人創造更多就業機會是必要的。他也希望藉此減少美國的貿易逆差，即一個國家購買他國商品的價值與其銷售給他國商品價值之間的差額。

paragraphs.en: This is not the first time the Trump administration has used tariffs as a tool for trade. Earlier this year, the US Supreme Court ruled that a previous set of taxes, called the “Liberation Day” tariffs, were illegal. Because of that ruling, the government is now using a different legal path to introduce these new charges. Chang Pao-Li, an economics lecturer at Singapore Management University, told BBC Business that this new approach is built on a “stronger legal foundation.” She noted that the government is now using its authority to investigate and respond to specific trade practices, which has been done successfully in the past.
paragraphs.zh: 這並非川普政府首次將關稅作為貿易工具。今年稍早，美國最高法院裁定先前的一套稅收（稱為「解放日」關稅）為非法。由於該項裁決，政府目前正透過不同的法律途徑來引入這些新收費。新加坡管理大學經濟學講師張寶莉 (Chang Pao-Li) 向 BBC 商業新聞表示，這種新方法建立在「更穩固的法律基礎」之上。她指出，政府目前正運用其權力來調查並回應特定的貿易行為，這在過去曾成功執行過。

paragraphs.en: Despite the government’s goals, the announcement has caused concern among many experts. Economists warn that these tariffs could make life more expensive for regular people. If companies have to pay more to bring goods into the US, they will often pass those extra costs on to their customers. This can lead to inflation, which is a general rise in the price of goods and services over time. Furthermore, experts worry that these actions could slow down global trade, making it harder for countries to work together on economic issues.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管政府有其目標，但這項公告已引起許多專家的擔憂。經濟學家警告，這些關稅可能會讓一般民眾的生活成本變得更高。如果企業必須支付更多費用才能將商品運入美國，他們通常會將這些額外成本轉嫁給消費者。這可能導致通貨膨脹，即商品和服務價格隨時間普遍上漲。此外，專家擔心這些行動可能會拖累全球貿易，使各國在經濟議題上更難以合作。

paragraphs.en: It is important to note that these new taxes are not expected to start immediately. BBC Business reports that the plan must go through a period of public consultation and potential hearings before it can be put into action. This means the rules will likely not take effect until next year. During this time, the government will listen to feedback from businesses and other groups that might be affected by the changes. Even after they are finalized, the tariffs will almost certainly face legal challenges in court, as many companies and international partners may try to stop or change them.
paragraphs.zh: 值得注意的是，這些新稅預計不會立即實施。BBC 商業新聞報導指出，該計畫在付諸實行前，必須經過一段時間的公眾諮詢與潛在的聽證會。這意味著這些規則很可能要到明年才會生效。在此期間，政府將聽取企業及其他可能受此變動影響的團體所提供的意見。即便在最終定案後，這些關稅幾乎肯定會面臨法律挑戰，因為許多企業與國際夥伴可能會試圖阻止或變更這些措施。

paragraphs.en: Ultimately, this situation highlights a difficult balance for the US government. While the administration believes that these taxes will protect American industry and fix long-standing trade imbalances, the global economy is deeply connected. Many businesses rely on parts and materials from all over the world to build their products. If these materials become more expensive, it could change how companies operate and how much consumers pay at the store. As the US moves forward with this policy, the world will be watching closely to see how other nations respond and what the long-term impact will be on the global economy.
paragraphs.zh: 歸根究柢，這種情況凸顯了美國政府面臨的兩難。雖然政府認為這些稅收將能保護美國產業並解決長期的貿易失衡，但全球經濟是緊密相連的。許多企業依賴來自世界各地的零件與原料來製造產品。如果這些原料變得更昂貴，可能會改變企業的運作方式以及消費者在商店支付的金額。隨著美國持續推動這項政策，全球將密切關注其他國家如何回應，以及這對全球經濟將產生何種長期影響。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To create a situation where everyone has the same fair chance of success.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是一個常見的商業與政治慣用語，字面上是「把球場弄平」，意指消除不公平的優勢。文中：Jamieson Greer from the USTR stated that these new tariffs are designed to “level the playing field” for American workers.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To give costs or charges to someone else, usually customers.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 將（成本或費用）轉嫁給他人。
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡的 pass on 不是「傳遞」的意思，而是指企業將增加的成本轉嫁給消費者。文中：If companies have to pay more to bring goods into the US, they will often pass those extra costs on to their customers.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To start using a plan or system; to make something effective.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是一個常見的片語，用來描述計畫從「紙上談兵」轉為「實際執行」。文中：BBC Business reports that the plan must go through a period of public consultation and potential hearings before it can be put into action.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the primary reason the US government is implementing these new tariffs?

options.A: To immediately reduce the national debt by collecting fees from foreign governments.
options.B: To create a fairer competitive environment for American workers and manufacturing.
options.C: To punish countries that have recently violated international trade laws in court.
options.D: To replace the 'Liberation Day' tariffs that were deemed too expensive for businesses.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第二段明確指出，USTR 的代表 Jamieson Greer 表示這些關稅旨在「level the playing field」（創造公平競爭環境），以幫助美國工人和製造業。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章提到的是減少貿易逆差而非國家債務；選項 C 錯誤，因為之前的關稅是被裁定違法，而非這些國家違反了國際法；選項 D 錯誤，因為「Liberation Day」關稅是被法院判定違法，並非為了替換其成本。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the potential impact of these tariffs on the average American consumer?

options.A: Consumers will benefit from a wider variety of locally produced goods.
options.B: Consumers will likely see an increase in the prices of daily goods and services.
options.C: Consumers will be protected from the effects of global inflation.
options.D: Consumers will pay fewer taxes directly to the government due to the new tariffs.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據第五段，經濟學家警告若企業必須支付更高的關稅，他們通常會將這些額外成本轉嫁給消費者，進而導致通貨膨脹，使生活成本變高。選項 A 無法由文中推論；選項 C 與文意相反，文章指出關稅可能導致通貨膨脹；選項 D 錯誤，關稅是企業支付給政府的進口費用，並非直接減免消費者的個人稅務。

quiz.question: In the context of the second paragraph, what does the phrase 'level the playing field' mean?

options.A: To build new factories on flat land for better construction.
options.B: To decrease the physical size of international trade zones.
options.C: To ensure that all competitors follow the same fair rules.
options.D: To lower the taxes for all countries to the same base rate.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。在商業與經濟語境中，「level the playing field」是一個慣用語，意指消除不公平的競爭優勢，讓所有參與者在相同的規則下競爭。選項 A 是字面意思的誤解；選項 B 與物理空間無關；選項 D 錯誤，因為文章提到不同國家面臨不同的稅率（如中國 40%，歐盟 20%），並非統一稅率。

quiz.question: What is the central theme of this article regarding the new US tariff policy?

options.A: A detailed guide on how businesses can avoid paying new import taxes.
options.B: A report on the legal success of the Trump administration's trade policies.
options.C: An analysis of how global trade works and why it is currently failing.
options.D: An overview of the proposed US tariffs, their goals, and the potential risks involved.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。整篇文章結構完整，涵蓋了政策內容（關稅）、政府目的（保護製造業）、潛在風險（通貨膨脹與經濟影響）以及未來程序（諮詢與法律挑戰），提供了全面的概覽。選項 A 內容文中未提及；選項 B 過於偏頗，文章也提到了專家的擔憂與法律挑戰；選項 C 過於廣泛，文章焦點在於美國的新關稅政策，而非全球貿易失敗的全面分析。
